Question:
Suppose \(f(x)\) is defined for all real numbers \(x;\) \(f(x)\gt0\) for all \(x;\) and \(f(a)f(b)=f(a+b)\) for all \(a\) and \(b.\) Which of the following statements are true?

I. \(f(0)=1\)

II. \(f(-a)=\frac{1}{f(a)}\) for all \(a\)

III. \(f(a)=\sqrt[3]{f(3a)}\) for all \(a\)

IV. \(f(b)\gt f(a)\) if \(b\gt a\)
